title: Databricks SQL
description: A Databricks workspace's Unity Catalog tables, read through a SQL warehouse with a personal access token.

fields.name: workspace
fields.label: Workspace
fields.help: The workspace's URL, its server hostname, or the warehouse's JDBC URL.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.label: SQL warehouse
fields.help: Its HTTP path or its ID; taken from the JDBC URL when one was pasted above.

fields.name: catalog
fields.label: Catalog
fields.help: The catalog to read; the workspace's default catalog when empty.

fields.name: schemas
fields.label: Schemas
fields.help: Which schemas to read (comma-separated); every schema it may see in the catalog when empty.

setup.title: Your workspace and SQL warehouse
setup.say:
In Databricks, open SQL Warehouses → your warehouse → Connection details. Copy its Server hostname and HTTP path here — or paste its whole JDBC URL into Workspace, which holds both.

A serverless warehouse starts in seconds; a classic one may take a few minutes on the first query.

fix.say: That does not look like a workspace address. Copy the URL from your browser while in Databricks, or the Server hostname from the warehouse's Connection details.

fix.when: give the SQL warehouse|is not a SQL warehouse
fix.say: Give the warehouse's HTTP path (/sql/1.0/warehouses/…) from its Connection details, or its ID.
No workspace answers at that address. Check it against your browser's address bar in Databricks; if the workspace allows only known addresses (IP access lists), let the engine's machine in.

setup.title: A user that may only read
setup.say: Superatom only reads. Give it a user or service principal of its own that may read and nothing more: on the warehouse, Permissions → Can use; in the catalog, run the commands below (name your catalog and the user). Then, signed in as it, make a token: your name (top right) → Settings → Developer → Access tokens → Generate new token.

copy.label: Read-only access to a catalog (Unity Catalog)

fix.when: refused the sign-in|401|invalid access token|Credential was not sent
fix.say: Databricks refused the token: it is mistyped, expired or revoked. Make a new one (Settings → Developer → Access tokens) and paste it whole.
Signed in, but this user may not use the warehouse. On the warehouse, Permissions → add the user with Can use.
There is no warehouse with that ID in this workspace. Copy its HTTP path again from its Connection details.
There is no catalog {catalog}, or this user may not use it: GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG {catalog} TO the user.

setup.title: Which schemas
setup.say: Leave it empty to read every schema it may see in the catalog, or name the ones to read (sales, finance). The check counts the tables it may read there.

fix.say: Signed in, but this user may read no table there. Grant it USE SCHEMA and SELECT (the commands in the step before), or name a schema it may read.
